svg.title: One server, six configuration files, three different top-level keys
svg.desc: A single knowledge-base server sits in the middle, drawn in the series accent colour, offering search_docs, get_doc and list_topics. Six host applications surround it, three on each side, each drawn with a blue spine to mark it as the client end of the wire. Every host card names its configuration file and, in a chip, the top-level JSON key that file must use. Claude Desktop with claude_desktop_config.json, Claude Code with .mcp.json, Cursor with .cursor/mcp.json and Gemini CLI with .gemini/settings.json all use mcpServers. VS Code with .vscode/mcp.json uses servers, and Zed with settings.json uses context_servers; those two chips are outlined in the warning colour and carry a triangle to mark them as differing from the majority. Each card also carries one short note: Claude Desktop is stdio only and takes remote servers as connectors, Claude Code requires a type field for remote entries, Cursor interpolates environment variables behind an env namespace, VS Code requires type on every entry, Gemini CLI has no type field at all and infers the transport from which key you used, and Zed documents no interpolation. A seventh client, a Python script, sits directly below the server with no configuration file at all. Arrows run from every client into the server. A footnote states that both key differences are silent, because an unrecognized top-level key reads as an empty server list rather than as an error, and that every arrow carries the same JSON-RPC 2.0 over the same two transports, with not one line of server code changing between them.
svg.text: One server. Six configuration files. Three top-level keys.
The wire is identical down every arrow. The first line of every file is not.
stdio only; remote is a connector
A triangle marks a top-level key that differs from the majority. Both differences are silent:
an unrecognized key reads as an empty server list, not as an error.
Every arrow above carries the same JSON-RPC 2.0 over the same two transports.
Not one line of server code changes between them.
